name: Bondye
note: The remote, supreme creator God of Haitian Vodou (from French 'Bon Dieu'); identified with the Christian God, served indirectly through the lwa. Living tradition; modern.

name: The Lwa
note: Collective hub for the lwa (mistè), the served spirits who mediate between Bondye and humanity, organized in nanchon (chiefly Rada and Petwo). Living tradition.

name: Rada nanchon
dom: cool, beneficent spirits; ancestral Dahomean rite
note: The Rada nanchon: 'cool' (dou) lwa of largely Fon/Dahomean derivation, served in the Rada rite. Publicly documented organizing category. Living tradition.

name: Petwo nanchon
note: The Petwo (Petro) nanchon: 'hot' (cho) lwa of New-World and Kongo derivation, served in the Petwo rite. Publicly documented organizing category. Living tradition.

name: Papa Legba
dom: crossroads; gates; opener of the way
note: Rada lwa, the gatekeeper opening the way between worlds; saluted first in ceremony. Publicly identified in Vodou imagery with St Peter (keys) and St Lazarus. Living tradition.

name: Erzulie Freda
note: Rada lwa of love and beauty; her chromolithograph is widely the Mater Dolorosa. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Erzulie Dantor
note: Petwo lwa, fierce protective mother; popularly imaged as the Black Madonna of Częstochowa (and St Barbara). Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Damballa Wedo
dom: serpent; creation; sky; purity; ancestral wisdom
note: Rada serpent lwa, ancient and benevolent creator-associated spirit, consort of Ayida-Wedo; popularly imaged as St Patrick (serpents). Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Ayida-Wedo
note: Rada rainbow-serpent lwa, consort of Damballa; the serpent pair embodies cosmic balance. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Baron Samedi
dom: death; cemeteries; the dead; healing of the dying
note: Chief of the Gede; lord of cemeteries and the dead, associated with the cemetery cross. Publicly attested. Living tradition; not modeled here as a 'narco-saint' or sensationalized figure.

name: The Gede
dom: the dead; ancestors; fertility; ribald humor
note: Family (and Petwo-adjacent nanchon) of lwa of death and the ancestors, led by the Barons and Maman Brigitte. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Maman Brigitte
dom: death; cemeteries; consort of Baron; protector of graves
note: Gede lwa, consort of Baron Samedi, mistress of the cemetery; her name reflects the Irish Brigid heritage of the diaspora. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Ogou
dom: iron; war; fire; soldiers; political power
note: Lwa of iron and war (Yoruba-derived Ogun), served across nanchon; popularly imaged as St James the Greater (Santiago Matamoros). Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Agwe
dom: the sea; ships; sovereign of the waters
note: Rada lwa, sovereign of the sea and patron of sailors and fishermen, consort of La Sirène. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: La Sirène
dom: the sea; wealth; music; mermaid spirit
note: Lwa of the sea, a mermaid spirit linked to Agwe and to the water-mother complex (Lasirèn/Labalèn). Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: The Marassa
note: The sacred Marassa (divine twins), among the first lwa served; popularly imaged as Sts Cosmas and Damian. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Loko
dom: sacred trees; healing; patron of priests (oungan)
note: Rada lwa of vegetation and healing, patron of the priesthood and of the poto-mitan/sacred tree, consort of Ayizan. Publicly attested. Living tradition.

name: Simbi
note: Lwa (Kongo-derived, often Petwo) of fresh water, springs and rain, associated with magic and patronage of healers/sorcerers. Publicly attested. Living tradition.
